title: Level 4 (Expert) - D-24
notes:
West leads the ♥K against 4♠. West wins the first trick and plays a second round of hearts which is ruffed in the dummy. The ♠A is cashed and East wins the second round of spades while West discards. East plays another heart, forcing South to ruff in hand.

It appears that, for South to have a chance, he needs West to hold the ♣Q and ♣J and for diamonds to be 3-3. South leads a club, West splits his honors, and dummy wins. 4 rounds of diamonds come next. If East ruffs low on the 4th round (ruffing high makes things easy), South can overruff and finesse again in clubs, holding the defense to 1 more trick. On the 4th round of diamonds, however, East will discard his remaining club and be sure to win 2 more trump tricks.

It is impossible for South to make 4♠ against best defense on this club layout. The only club distribution that gives South a chance is ♣QJ doubleton with either defender. South should cash the ♣A and ♣K early hoping the ♣Q and ♣J will fall. When East follows with the ♣Q and ♣J, the diamonds come next. If East ruffs the 4th round, South overruffs and leads a winning club. If instead East discards, South discards his last club and loses only 1 trump trick at the end.

If West was dealt the ♣QJ, South will see these cards fall under the ♣A and ♣K. In this case South must cash a third round of clubs followed by exactly 2 high diamonds. Dummy's winning club can now be played and East is held to a single trump trick as before.
